searchTitle: GTA 6 Game Sharing: PS5 and Xbox Licence Rules
excerpt: Check GTA 6 console-sharing rules on PS5 and Xbox, including designated consoles, licence ownership, simultaneous play and account safety.

cover.alt: Two London apartments and their game consoles connected by a luminous library bridge beneath an ownership key.

intro: You can use the console-sharing features of PS5 and Xbox with eligible digital games, but sharing access does not transfer ownership of GTA 6. The useful question is which account owns the licence, which console has the sharing designation, and which person is trying to play. Treat those as three separate facts before following an account-swapping tutorial.
journalNote: I am interested in the entitlement design behind a shared living-room console: a downloaded file and a right to launch it are different pieces of state. This guide applies platform documentation rather than claiming a two-household GTA 6 play test.

sections.heading: Start with the account that actually bought the game
paragraphs: Open purchase history on the account you believe owns the game. A preorder confirmation, a downloaded icon and access through another person's console are not interchangeable evidence. Record the edition, platform and purchasing account privately. Do not post order identifiers or screenshots containing email addresses in a public support thread.

This matters in a household with several profiles. Someone can install a game while signed into one account and later open it from another. If sharing is not enabled for that console, the second profile may see a lock despite the files being present. Reinstalling downloads the same files; it does not change the owner of the licence.

sections.heading: PS5: understand the console designation
paragraphs: Sony calls the relevant feature Console Sharing and Offline Play. Its support page explains that enabling it on a PS5 lets eligible users on that console play purchased and downloaded games, including when that console is offline, subject to the applicable conditions. Only one PS5 can have this designation for an account at a time.

Use the documented settings on the console you intend to designate. Do not repeatedly toggle consoles to troubleshoot an unrelated network failure. If this is a second-hand console, check which account you are using rather than relying on a seller's promise that installed games will remain yours. A device sale does not automatically transfer another person's digital library.

paragraphs: Microsoft documents a device licence and a user licence in its product-sharing model. The home Xbox designation is central to shared access on a device; the owner's signed-in access on another device is a different path. The details can depend on the product and how it was acquired, so check the current consumer support instructions before changing a designation.

Keep the second player on their own profile. Saves, achievements, privacy settings and multiplayer identity should not become tangled just because the installation is shared. A shared game licence also does not manufacture an online multiplayer subscription or guarantee that every account-specific reward follows the second player.

You may also expose payment methods, recovery information and personal data by exchanging accounts. Buy through an authorised route and use official sharing features for their intended purpose. Do not disable two-factor authentication to make an unofficial arrangement easier.

Before buying an extra copy, separate a temporary service outage from a persistent entitlement restriction. Check the platform status, confirm purchase history, and follow the official licence troubleshooting steps. If support is needed, describe the profiles and console designations without sending passwords or recovery codes.

sections.heading: Read the platform line before the headline
paragraphs: Open the publisher's official GTA VI page directly and find the named platforms. Follow any product links from there. A console availability statement is evidence for those consoles; it is not a timetable for an additional platform. An unofficial article can correctly describe a trailer and still add an unsupported PC date in its headline.

Record the source date and the exact scope of the statement. If a PC announcement is published later, this article needs a substantive update with that source. sections.heading: Separate three things people call playing on PC
paragraphs: A native PC release runs the game software on your computer. Remote Play sends input to your own console and streams its video back. A cloud service runs the game on a provider's hardware, if the title and your account are eligible. The laptop screen can look similar in all three cases, but installation, ownership and performance responsibilities are different.

paragraphs: If the file has not been opened, leave it unexecuted and use your operating system's security tools to review or remove it. If you ran software, the response depends on what happened: credential entry, administrator permission and payment information all create different exposure. Use trusted security guidance for your system rather than downloading a second supposed cleanup utility from the same page.

If you entered an account password, change it through the service's official site from a trusted device and review active sessions and recovery settings. Contact the relevant provider if a purchase or payment account is involved. A reassuring filename or an antivirus result alone is not a guarantee that an installer is safe.

paragraphs: This is also a useful habit beyond gaming. A convincing interface can make an unsupported claim feel finished. paragraphs: A new official PC announcement, a publisher-linked PC store page or published PC requirements would materially change this guide. intro: Offline play is a combination of game requirements and platform licence conditions. A disc in your bag, a completed download and an offline-enabled console each answer a different question. Before relying on GTA 6 away from the internet, verify the current game requirements and test your own supported console setup while you can still fix a problem.
journalNote: This article is a planning and diagnostic guide, not a claim that I tested every GTA 6 mission without a connection. The useful engineering idea is to separate content availability from permission to execute it.

sections.heading: Decide what offline means for your session
paragraphs: Do you mean starting a single-player mode with no connection, resuming a save, or accessing an online feature during an outage? These are different tasks. Do not use a statement about a story mode to promise that network-dependent services will work without their servers. This guide does not invent a mode-by-mode compatibility list where the publisher has not supplied one.

Write down the exact edition, console and profile you plan to use. If the setup depends on another person's digital purchase, read the platform sharing conditions first. A test on the owner's console may not describe a second console's behaviour. For PS5, Sony's Console Sharing and Offline Play documentation is a relevant starting point for eligible digital purchases.

sections.heading: Installation is a content question
paragraphs: For GTA 6 specifically, Rockstar's November 18 platforms-and-editions FAQ says the boxed Standard Edition contains a digital download code and no disc. Treat that purchase as a code-redemption and digital-licence path. A box on a retailer's shelf is not evidence of playable physical media, and keeping that empty box nearby does not replace the account entitlement.

Check the console's installation and download queues. A playable-looking tile does not necessarily mean every component and required update has finished. Leave enough time for preparation before travelling; a download estimate from someone else's connection is not a reliable deadline for yours. Storage requirements can also change with updates.

For games generally, a genuine disc can have its own installation and access conditions. Do not import those assumptions into GTA 6's documented code-in-box edition. Read the exact product contents and code-redemption conditions instead of treating the word physical as a promise of a disc.

paragraphs: Start with a normal online launch and resolve any official required updates or account notices. Close the game normally. Then use the console's supported network controls to test the intended offline state. Launch using the same profile and installation you will take with you. Record the exact result; do not describe a menu opening as proof that every later feature works.

Afterwards, restore the connection and verify normal operation. Avoid deleting saves, unlinking accounts or factory-resetting the console as a first response to a failed test. Those actions can create additional recovery problems while leaving the original entitlement issue untouched. If the platform reports a licence error, follow its official troubleshooting path.

sections.heading: Know what the test cannot promise
paragraphs: A successful trial is evidence about that console, account, game version and supported action at that time. It is not an assurance against future patches, expired subscriptions, corrupted storage or changed account designations. If you move the sharing designation after testing, the earlier result may no longer describe your setup.

Cloud streaming is a separate case: the game runs elsewhere and the video must reach you over a connection. Remote Play also relies on a network path to your console. Neither is a substitute for an installed offline-capable local setup when your goal is playing somewhere without internet access.

paragraphs: The practical win is confidence based on a check you performed, not a blanket promise copied from a forum. For download scheduling, use the separate preload guide. For entitlement sharing between profiles, use the dedicated console-sharing article.

title: GTA 6 on Xbox One: Cloud Streaming Is Different From a Native Port
searchTitle: GTA 6 on Xbox One: Cloud Streaming, Not a Native Port
excerpt: Understand GTA 6 on Xbox One: distinguish a native release from eligible Xbox cloud streaming, and check title, plan, region and controller support.

cover.alt: An older console receives a luminous video stream from a distant server tower while a newer console renders beside a television.
cover.caption: Original GPT-generated pixel-art editorial illustration; conceptual artwork, not a product screenshot or test result.

intro: Seeing GTA 6 on an Xbox One screen does not establish that an Xbox One edition runs locally. A cloud service can send video to older hardware while the game executes on a remote machine. Check the exact official product and cloud eligibility information before treating a streaming option as a native port or buying a subscription for it.
journalNote: This is a system-design explanation of execution versus display. I have not measured GTA 6 cloud latency or image quality on an Xbox One, and this article does not present generated artwork as a gameplay capture.

sections.heading: Ask where the game process is running
paragraphs: There are three useful possibilities: the game runs on the device under the television, on another console you own, or on a cloud provider's hardware. The first is local play, the second is a remote-play arrangement, and the third is cloud streaming. They can share a controller and display while having very different purchase and network requirements.

An official listing for Xbox Series X or S is not a listing for a native Xbox One executable. Likewise, a web page showing a cloud play button is not evidence that an installation file exists for every device that can display the stream. Read the platform line and the access conditions together.

sections.heading: Check eligibility before paying
paragraphs: Rockstar's November 18 platforms FAQ explicitly announces Xbox Cloud Gaming access on Xbox Series X|S and Xbox One, using Series S graphics settings. That is the confirmed streaming route discussed here, not a native Xbox One release. Check Xbox's current account, plan, region and supported-client requirements before purchasing access.

Use the official Xbox GTA VI product page and follow its current service guidance. Availability can depend on region, subscription, ownership and supported client. A general statement that a service supports cloud gaming does not prove that a particular title is included for your account. Inspect the actual title while signed into your own account, without sharing credentials.

The Rockstar launch communication is a starting point for supported access paths, not an eternal guarantee about a subscription catalogue. If the product and cloud catalogue disagree, resolve that with official support before purchasing solely for one game. This guide intentionally avoids publishing a universal plan-and-region promise.

sections.heading: Work through the network path
paragraphs: For local execution, controller input reaches the local game and frames travel to the display. For cloud execution, input crosses the network, the remote machine processes it, and compressed video returns. Your experience can therefore change with network congestion, Wi-Fi conditions, service routing and encoding even if the remote hardware is powerful.

Bandwidth is only one part of that path. An advertised connection speed does not tell you the round-trip delay, packet loss or stability during the evening. Try a supported cloud session on your actual connection before making a hardware decision. If the service offers a network test, interpret it as evidence for that place and time.

Use an existing eligible session or a legitimate service test where available; do not buy an unknown account or a supposed compatibility patch. Try the controls and readability on the screen you actually plan to use. A phone test on a different network is not a complete Xbox One living-room test.

If the picture breaks up, compare a wired connection or a less congested local network before concluding the game itself is defective. If the service reports a queue or availability problem, record that message separately from network symptoms. A queue is an access-capacity issue, not evidence that the older console is rendering too slowly.

sections.heading: What not to download
paragraphs: Do not install an unofficial Xbox One conversion, emulator unlocker or firmware modification because a video claims to show the game on older hardware. Streaming can explain that video without any native port existing. A captured television screen alone tells you little about the machine producing its frames.

Keep the distinction in your own descriptions too. “I accessed a supported cloud session on this device” is precise. “The game has an Xbox One version” is a different claim requiring different evidence. That precision makes buying advice more useful and reduces the chance that another player spends money based on a misunderstanding.

title: GTA 6 on PS5 Pro: Why Sharper Graphics Do Not Automatically Mean 60 FPS
searchTitle: GTA 6 on PS5 Pro: Sharper Graphics vs 60 FPS
excerpt: Understand GTA 6 on PS5 Pro without confusing sharper output with 60 FPS. Separate reconstruction, CPU simulation, frame pacing and input latency.

cover.alt: A pixel-art graphics workshop with a sharp reconstructed city image on one display and a separate frame-timing conveyor beside a console.
cover.caption: Original GPT-generated pixel-art editorial illustration; conceptual artwork, not a product screenshot or test result.

intro: A sharper GTA 6 image on PS5 Pro does not by itself prove a 60 FPS mode. Resolution reconstruction, ray-tracing quality and frame rate solve different problems. Rockstar's launch information is the place to check supported modes; a television's refresh-rate label or an unofficial comparison video cannot establish the game's actual rendering cadence.
journalNote: I think about performance as a complete frame pipeline, much as I would diagnose a slow interface. This is a technical explainer grounded in release information, not an instrumented PS5 Pro benchmark or a claim that I captured frame times.

sections.heading: Read a graphics promise literally
paragraphs: Rockstar's launch communication discusses a 30 FPS target and PS5 Pro image enhancements. Check that source for the current wording and supported modes. A claim about sharper output or improved shadows is not a separate claim about a doubled frame rate. If the publisher later adds another mode, the correct update is to document it with a date and source.

This is particularly important in launch-week comparison posts. A headline may combine several true statements into a false implication: more powerful hardware, reconstruction technology and a high-refresh television do not jointly prove that a specific game runs at a particular frame rate.

sections.heading: Understand the frame budget
paragraphs: At a steady 30 FPS, successive frames are about 33.3 milliseconds apart. At 60 FPS, that interval is about 16.7 milliseconds. Those are arithmetic intervals, not measured GTA 6 results. Reaching the shorter interval requires the critical work for each frame to fit into it consistently. Improving only image reconstruction may leave simulation or other work as the limiting stage.

A city-scale game can involve world simulation, animation, visibility work, rendering and presentation. The exact bottleneck depends on its implementation and scene. Without profiling data, it is speculation to declare a particular subsystem responsible. The useful lesson is simply that performance is a pipeline rather than one number on a GPU specification sheet.

paragraphs: Reconstruction can create a higher-resolution output from a lower-resolution input. Its visual quality depends on the algorithm, source data, motion and integration. paragraphs: A credible test names the console, game version, graphics mode, display settings and capture method. It uses comparable scenes and explains whether the footage measures unique rendered frames or merely records an output signal. Compression can hide image differences; a still image can hide pacing problems. Prefer analysis that makes those limitations visible.

If someone reports input latency, look for the input device, display mode and measurement method. A frame-rate counter is not a complete end-to-end latency measurement. Likewise, a short average FPS figure can hide a few disruptive long frames. The right evidence depends on the claim being made.

sections.heading: Choose hardware around your actual priorities
paragraphs: If you already own a supported console, start with the official mode information and reliable comparisons before upgrading for this one title. Decide whether you care most about image clarity, particular effects, motion or the wider library. Do not pay for an assumed 60 FPS mode merely because the hardware could run other games at that rate.

For a new purchase, compare the complete cost, including the edition, required accessories and any disc-drive choice. A technically better image may matter to you; that remains a preference rather than proof of a higher frame rate. Start with the official publisher and platform information. Confirm that the title supports the route, that your client is supported, and that your account has the required entitlement. A working internet connection cannot fix an unavailable cloud title. Owning a game cannot fix an unsupported client by itself.

intro: Before the first mission, spend a few minutes making the game readable, audible and comfortable for you. This GTA 6 accessibility checklist explains what to look for and how to test it. sections.heading: Start from the barrier, not a menu screenshot
paragraphs: A small label, an unclear sound cue and a difficult button combination are different problems. Name the action that is hard: reading an objective, distinguishing a marker, following dialogue or holding a control. That gives you a reason to inspect a setting and a concrete way to judge whether it helped.

Use your ordinary seating distance, lighting and audio arrangement. A screenshot enlarged on a laptop can conceal a readability problem on the television. If someone else helps with setup, keep the player's preference central. Accessibility is not a competition to use the fewest assists or the most difficult controls.

sections.heading: Text and visual information
paragraphs: Look for available controls affecting subtitle presentation, text size, contrast, interface scale and visual cues. Their names and availability must be checked in the actual game or official guide. Do not assume that a subtitle adjustment changes every menu label, map annotation or objective prompt.

Test a real task after making a change. Can you read the objective quickly without leaning forward? Can you distinguish important information without relying on one colour alone? If a cue is still ambiguous, note where it occurs. That is more actionable feedback than simply saying the interface is hard to see.

intro: A sandbox label on one Tether capability does not mean every command launched by Tether runs inside that sandbox. The Tether changelog explicitly distinguishes local MCP command execution from the workspace sandbox. Before adding a stdio server, inspect what that process can access as the operating-system user that launches it.
journalNote: This is a permission-model walkthrough based on the public Tether changelog and MCP documentation. It does not disclose UltraFit360's private tool configuration or claim a full security audit of Tether.

sections.heading: Make a process inventory before a tool list
paragraphs: Write down the browser, WebUI service, Tether process, model backend and each local MCP server. For each process, record where it runs and which account launches it. A list of friendly tool names omits the detail that controls access: the executable, arguments, environment and operating-system privileges.

For a downloaded server, inspect its publisher and supported installation route. Pin the package version or other reproducible reference where possible. A legitimate project can still have more access than your task needs; popularity is not a permission boundary. Avoid copying a configuration that silently invokes an unrelated shell command.

sections.heading: Separate workspace controls from operating-system controls
paragraphs: A workspace sandbox can restrict covered operations to a defined area, but a separately launched process may inherit different rights. Tether's changelog is important precisely because it describes that distinction for local MCP commands. Do not infer that restrictions on a terminal or workspace tool automatically wrap every child service.

The operating-system account may be able to read home-directory files, environment variables, mounted folders and network resources. The effective access depends on how you run the process. A narrow working directory is not the same as a filesystem restriction; it tells a process where it starts, not necessarily where it can go.

paragraphs: A server launched from a developer shell can inherit variables that were intended for other work. Supply only the values the server actually needs, and keep them out of public configuration examples. Logs can also disclose sensitive paths or inputs even if the final answer is clean.

If a tool needs network access, identify its intended destinations and authentication path. If it does not, consider a supported environment that restricts unnecessary egress. This is a deployment decision, not a claim that a prompt can enforce network isolation. Test the actual setup rather than relying on a diagram.

sections.heading: Fail closed and keep a removal path
paragraphs: The changelog describes sandbox behaviour for supported systems, but platform and version details matter. A failure to initialise a security feature should not become an undocumented reason to rerun everything with wider permissions. Stop, collect non-sensitive diagnostics and follow the supported remedy for that release.

Before enabling a server for everyday use, know how to disable it, revoke its credentials and remove its pairing. Recheck access after upgrades or configuration changes. The safe mental model is a collection of processes with explicit permissions, not a single trusted bubble around everything an AI interface can do.

faqs.question: Are all Tether MCP commands inside the workspace sandbox?
faqs.answer: No blanket guarantee is justified. The public changelog distinguishes local MCP commands from the workspace sandbox; inspect the installed version and the permissions of each launched process.

faqs.question: Is stdio automatically safe because it has no public port?
faqs.answer: No. Stdio avoids a network-listener requirement, but the server process can still access resources allowed by its operating-system account and configuration.

faqs.question: Should I test with real secrets to see whether a tool can read them?
faqs.answer: No. Use a disposable environment and clearly invented canary files. Testing the permission boundary does not require exposing actual credentials or customer data.

intro: When Open Terminal fails in Tether on Windows, first find out which process failed to start. Use ordinary local diagnostics with no secrets in the output you share. For example, PowerShell's Get-Command can tell you which executable a command name resolves to. Do not dump the entire environment into a public issue; developer machines often contain unrelated credentials.

Be especially careful with fixes that disable a sandbox, relax filesystem permissions or elevate the entire process. They can make the symptom disappear by changing the security model. paragraphs: A useful report contains the expected action, actual result, exact versions, minimal steps and sanitised error text. Say whether the shell works outside Tether and whether the same test fails in a disposable workspace. If you tried a documented upgrade, name that version and its observed result.

Remove usernames, private repository paths, pairing material and customer content. Keep enough structure to diagnose the problem: replacing an entire stack trace with “error” defeats the exercise, while exposing every environment variable is unnecessary. paragraphs: Repeat the original harmless terminal action using the intended ordinary account and security setup. Then restart the relevant process and repeat it again to catch a fix that only worked in one inherited shell environment. Save the working version and configuration notes privately.

faqs.question: Should I run Tether as administrator when its terminal fails?
faqs.answer: Do not make elevation the default fix. Identify the failing component and follow the installed release's guidance; wider privileges can hide a configuration problem while increasing access.

faqs.question: Does a working PowerShell window prove Tether can launch it?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Tether may run under a different environment, user context, executable path or security boundary. Compare those conditions before drawing a conclusion.

faqs.question: What should a public bug report include?
faqs.answer: Include versions, Windows details, the exact operation, a minimal reproduction and sanitised error text. Exclude pairing secrets, private paths, environment values and real prompt content.

intro: Before upgrading to vLLM 0.34, inspect your launch configuration, checkpoint compatibility, dependencies and GPU image. sections.heading: Inventory what you are actually running

Include custom parsers, logits processors, quantisation choices and adapters because those can be the parts an ordinary chat smoke test misses.

Consult the release's upgrade table for the exact features your deployment uses; this article is a gate checklist, not a replacement for that table.

One direct check is an old VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 setting. The release says that setting now fails at startup. title: vLLM Extensible KV Cache: Measure Throughput and Latency Separately

intro: A larger KV cache can help a server handle more work without making every individual answer faster. When evaluating vLLM's extensible KV cache, measure aggregate throughput and interactive latency separately. The useful result is a workload-specific trade-off, not a single speedup number detached from model, hardware and concurrency.
journalNote: The diagram is explanatory, and the timing examples are arithmetic fixtures. This article contains no invented GPU measurements and does not turn vLLM's release-note benchmarks into results from our own infrastructure.

sections.heading: Understand what is being stored
paragraphs: During autoregressive generation, the KV cache retains attention-related state so the model does not recompute all earlier state for every generated token. Its footprint depends on model architecture, context, active sequences and implementation details. It is not interchangeable with the model weights or the operating system's file cache.

The vLLM 0.34 release describes an extensible cache sized from memory available after warmup. Review the exact release notes and tuning documentation before changing defaults. A deployment sharing a GPU with other processes has a different memory situation from an otherwise idle dedicated device.

sections.heading: Define the question before collecting numbers
paragraphs: For a coding assistant, a useful question might be whether short interactive requests remain responsive while several long contexts are active. For a batch job, completed work per unit time may matter more. These are different acceptance criteria, so do not select a metric only after seeing which one improved.

Write down the model revision, quantisation, GPU, runtime version, context limits and workload distribution. Keep them fixed across the comparison unless the change is explicitly part of the experiment. Include a warmup procedure and distinguish startup from steady-state service.

sections.heading: Use a transparent arithmetic example
paragraphs: Suppose an invented request starts at zero, emits its first token at 0.8 seconds and finishes at 2.8 seconds with 21 output tokens. A simple post-first-token average is two seconds divided by 20 intervals, or 0.1 seconds per interval. This is a teaching calculation, not a vLLM benchmark or a claim about a particular GPU.

The denominator matters. Dividing by all 21 tokens gives a different number. State the method, especially when comparing a tool that defines per-token timing differently. A polished chart cannot repair mismatched definitions between two runs.

sections.heading: Sweep concurrency without moving every other variable
paragraphs: Run the same workload at a few deliberate concurrency levels and retain raw per-request results. Separate short and long prompts if their behaviour differs. Use repeated runs and report variability rather than one best attempt. Do not hide a configuration that fails only at the highest offered load.

If you compare cache modes or settings, use the supported options for the exact vLLM version and record their effective values. A cache improvement may increase completed work while changing decode timing. Whether that is acceptable depends on the service's latency and reliability targets, not on a universal ranking.

sections.heading: Turn results into a deployment decision
paragraphs: Choose the configuration that meets your actual constraints: interactive delay, completion reliability, cost and capacity. If a larger cache helps batch throughput but harms an important interactive path, consider workload separation or admission control rather than presenting the throughput gain as a blanket win.

Publish the test method and limitations with any future chart. Until measurements exist, use a conceptual diagram such as this article's figure. It communicates the trade-off without manufacturing numerical evidence that readers might use to buy hardware or size a service.

faqs.question: Does a bigger KV cache always reduce latency?
faqs.answer: No. Capacity, batching, concurrency and decode behaviour interact. Measure first-token and per-token timing under your representative workload instead of inferring latency from cache size.

faqs.question: Are the performance figures in vLLM release notes our results?
faqs.answer: No. They are the project's reported results under its stated conditions. This guide describes how to run and label a separate comparison without claiming those measurements as ours.

faqs.question: Should failed requests count in a benchmark?
faqs.answer: Yes. Report attempts, completed requests and failures. A throughput figure that quietly drops OOMs or timeouts can make an unreliable configuration look faster.

searchTitle: vLLM OOM After Startup: A Memory Triage Guide
excerpt: Diagnose vLLM OOMs after a successful startup by separating weights, KV cache, concurrency and other GPU users. Build a small, reproducible failure case.

cover.alt: A pixel-art GPU with separate labelled-by-shape memory compartments for weights, active context and runtime overhead, inspected at a repair bench.
cover.caption: Original GPT-generated pixel-art editorial illustration; conceptual artwork, not a product screenshot or test result.

intro: A vLLM server can start successfully and still run out of memory when requests arrive. Loading weights proves that one startup phase fit; it does not prove that your longest prompt, largest output and highest concurrency fit together. Diagnose the workload that crosses the boundary before choosing a larger GPU or changing several settings at once.
journalNote: This is a workload-reduction method based on vLLM's memory documentation. It contains no claim that a particular model fits a particular card, and the memory diagram is conceptual rather than a measured allocation capture.

sections.heading: Identify the phase that fails
paragraphs: Collect the first relevant error and note whether failure occurs during model load, warmup, the first short request, a long request or concurrent traffic. Preserve the version and effective launch settings. These phases point to different hypotheses; a generic screenshot saying out of memory is not enough to choose one.

Use invented prompts for reproduction. Do not copy a real user's long conversation into an issue report. You usually need the input length and request shape, not the confidential words, to reproduce a capacity boundary. Keep a private record of sensitive configuration separately from a sanitised support packet.

sections.heading: Check the whole device, not only the server process
paragraphs: Inspect GPU memory use with the tools appropriate to your platform. Another model service, notebook or desktop workload may be sharing the device. Record what is running before deciding that the new vLLM version alone caused the failure. Do not terminate unknown processes on a shared system without understanding their owners.

Then distinguish weights, runtime overhead and request-dependent state. Quantisation can affect weight storage but does not automatically eliminate every other allocation. A smaller download or lower-bit checkpoint is not a universal guarantee that a workload will fit.

sections.heading: Reduce to one short, bounded request
paragraphs: Begin with one harmless short prompt and a small explicit output limit through the supported API. If that fails, investigate the baseline configuration and runtime before adding load. If it succeeds, increase one dimension at a time: input length, output limit or concurrency.

This produces a boundary you can describe. For example, “one short request works, but two long-context requests fail” is a useful observation. Do not replace it with an invented universal token limit; the result applies to the measured model, runtime and device combination.

sections.heading: Change supported settings deliberately
paragraphs: Consult the exact version's memory-conservation and optimisation guides. Context limits, concurrency controls, supported quantisation and parallelism options have different consequences. A setting that reduces memory can also change quality, latency or deployment complexity. Record that trade-off rather than describing every reduction as a free improvement.

For vLLM 0.34, changed cache defaults make old tuning assumptions particularly worth reviewing. Do not carry a flag from an earlier release without checking its current meaning. Also avoid blindly raising a memory-utilisation value after an OOM; first understand what the runtime is allocating and what else shares the GPU.

sections.heading: Preserve an application-level limit
paragraphs: Even after finding a stable test, bound the input and output sizes your application accepts. Apply admission control to concurrency and reject or queue excess work in a deliberate way. A UI that allows unlimited prompt growth can eventually exceed a server that looked healthy during a small smoke test.

Handle failure visibly: return a useful retry or capacity message without exposing internal paths. Avoid an unlimited retry loop that resubmits the same oversized request. Retrying an unchanged impossible workload can amplify load without making it fit.

sections.heading: Verify the fix against the original boundary
paragraphs: Repeat the minimal failing case, then a representative workload with the chosen limits. Record attempts, completions and failures alongside memory and timing observations. A single successful request after a restart is weaker evidence than a repeatable test at the intended load.

Keep the previous compatible deployment and a rollback criterion if this began after an upgrade. The result you want is an explained capacity limit and a controlled application behaviour, not a ritual of restarting the process whenever a large request arrives.

faqs.question: Why can vLLM start and then OOM on the first request?
faqs.answer: Request processing can require memory beyond the loaded weights, including context-related state and runtime allocations. Identify the exact failing phase and workload rather than treating startup as a capacity test.

faqs.question: Will reducing concurrency always fix an OOM?
faqs.answer: No. It is a useful isolation test, but a single long request, unsupported configuration, runtime allocation or another GPU process may still exceed the available budget.

faqs.question: Can I use model file size as the full VRAM requirement?
faqs.answer: No. File size does not account for every runtime representation, KV cache, execution overhead or other process. Use the runtime's documented sizing and actual observations.

title: TTFT, TPOT and Tokens per Second: Benchmark a Local Coding Model Honestly
searchTitle: TTFT, TPOT and Tokens per Second: An Honest LLM Benchmark
excerpt: Measure local LLM responsiveness with TTFT, per-token timing and throughput. Use monotonic clocks, fixed workloads and explicit failure counts.

cover.alt: A pixel-art timing laboratory where the first token arrives at one clock and later tokens travel along a separate conveyor.
cover.caption: Original GPT-generated pixel-art editorial illustration; conceptual artwork, not a product screenshot or test result.

intro: Tokens per second is not a complete description of a local coding model. A model can start late and then decode quickly, or start quickly and stream slowly. Measure time to first token, the timing after that first token, full completion time and throughput under a declared workload. Report failures too.
journalNote: The worked timing fixture below is intentionally synthetic and can be checked with ordinary JavaScript. It explains the calculation; it is not evidence about a GPU, model ranking or our private AI coach.

sections.heading: Choose the user experience you are measuring
paragraphs: For an interactive code assistant, the delay before useful output matters. For a background batch, completed work over a time interval may dominate. Write down the question before running the benchmark so you do not select a favourable metric afterwards.

Specify the model revision, quantisation, hardware, runtime, context limits and test inputs. Keep cold loading separate from warm inference. If one run loads the model from disk and another reuses a warm process, the comparison measures more than model-generation speed.

sections.heading: Use a monotonic clock and a clear start point
paragraphs: A monotonic timer is suited to elapsed intervals because wall-clock adjustments should not change a duration. Define when timing starts: entering an application queue, sending an HTTP request or starting server execution. Client and server timings can both be useful, but they answer different questions.

In streaming APIs, a keep-alive or metadata event is not necessarily a generated token. Inspect the protocol and identify the first actual output event. Use the provider's reported token count or a documented compatible counting method; do not treat each network chunk as exactly one token.

paragraphs: Retain raw request observations so you can compute a median and tail values rather than only an average. A few long waits can matter disproportionately in an interactive product. State the number of attempts and how many completed, timed out or failed.

sections.heading: Distinguish throughput from per-request speed
paragraphs: Aggregate throughput divides completed output by a declared observation interval. It can rise when a server batches more requests even if an individual request becomes slower. State whether the interval includes warmup, queue drain and failures. Different measurement windows can produce different-looking totals from the same workload.

Do not multiply one request's speed by a concurrency setting and call that measured server capacity. Run the concurrent workload and observe it. If you cannot run the hardware, publish the method or a clearly labelled simulation rather than a fabricated ranking chart.

sections.heading: Keep answer quality in the experiment
paragraphs: A coding model that returns invalid code quickly has not necessarily improved the product. Use a fixed set of tasks with meaningful checks such as compilation, tests, schema validation or a reviewed expected behaviour. Keep those quality results beside timing and cost.

Also distinguish model execution from the complete agent workflow. Tool calls, retries, repository inspection and test execution add time and can improve correctness. A raw decoding benchmark does not describe that whole workflow. Report the boundary you actually measured.

sections.heading: Publish enough detail to reproduce the claim
paragraphs: Include configuration, workload, counting method, timing definitions and failure counts with any future results. Use charts generated from the retained data, not image-generated bars. The strongest benchmark is one whose limitations a reader can understand before using it to choose a model or buy hardware.

faqs.question: What is TTFT?
faqs.answer: Time to first token is the interval from the chosen request start to the first observed output token. State whether your measurement includes client queueing and network time.

faqs.question: How should I calculate TPOT?
faqs.answer: State your definition. One common post-first-token average divides completion time minus first-token time by the number of output tokens minus one, excluding cases with fewer than two output tokens.

faqs.question: Can I compare two published tokens-per-second numbers directly?
faqs.answer: Only with compatible definitions and conditions. Model, hardware, quantisation, prompt length, output length, concurrency, warmup and failure handling can all change the result.

title: The Old vLLM ROCm Image Is Gone: Make Your GPU Deployment Reproducible
searchTitle: vLLM ROCm Images: Build a Reproducible GPU Deployment
excerpt: An old vLLM ROCm image no longer exists? Check the release's supported runtime, host compatibility and immutable image reference before migrating.

cover.alt: A pixel-art server loading dock with an obsolete container crate and a new runtime crate checked against a compatibility ledger.
cover.caption: Original GPT-generated pixel-art editorial illustration; conceptual artwork, not a product screenshot or test result.

intro: If a deployment can no longer pull an old-style vLLM ROCm image, first check whether that artefact is still published for the target release. vLLM 0.34 changes its supported ROCm artefacts. Replacing a tag by guesswork is risky because the container runtime, host driver, GPU architecture and model support must still fit together.
journalNote: This is an artefact and compatibility guide, separate from the broader vLLM upgrade checklist. I have not tested an AMD hardware matrix, and a successful image pull is not presented as proof of inference compatibility.

sections.heading: Classify the error before changing the stack
paragraphs: A missing image tag, registry authentication failure, network timeout and runtime crash are different failures. Save the exact sanitised error. If the registry says a manifest is unknown, inspect the release's published artefacts; if access is denied, investigate authentication and repository visibility instead of renaming the image.

Do not paste registry credentials into an issue report. A public image can be discussed with its repository, tag and error wording without disclosing a private registry token. Keep your original deployment record so the attempted migration remains reversible.

sections.heading: Read the release's installation matrix
paragraphs: The v0.34.0 notes explicitly describe changes to ROCm artefacts. Use the release's installation instructions and supported wheel or image references. An old suffix copied from a previous release can fail because the project no longer publishes that combination, not because your machine suddenly lost internet access.

Avoid assuming that a newer ROCm-labelled image supports every older GPU or host configuration. Check the project's documented hardware and host requirements. The image bundles user-space components, while host drivers and device access remain part of the deployment environment.

sections.heading: Test on a separate deployment
paragraphs: Start with a disposable candidate environment and a harmless short request. Confirm that the intended GPU is used, not merely that an HTTP service responds. Then test the model features your application depends on, including streaming or structured output where relevant.

Only after basic correctness should you increase context and concurrency. Runtime changes can alter memory behaviour and kernel selection. If the test fails, preserve the first meaningful error and the exact stack record. Repeatedly editing tags without retaining results makes diagnosis slower.

sections.heading: Pin the working result, not just the package name
paragraphs: Once the candidate works, record the immutable image reference and application configuration together. Pin the model revision and compatible dependencies as appropriate. A deployment command that downloads an unspecified latest model on every start is not fully reproducible even if the container itself is pinned.

Keep secrets in the deployment's supported secret store rather than embedding them in the image or public command. Keep private network addresses out of a published tutorial. The public lesson is the compatibility method; it does not require exposing your production topology.

sections.heading: Make rollback a complete combination
paragraphs: Retain the previous compatible image, configuration and model assumptions. A rollback that restores only one layer can still fail if the host runtime or shared storage changed incompatibly. Document the recovery sequence and test it where practical before promotion.

Do not claim a performance improvement from an artefact migration until you measure the same workload under controlled conditions. First establish availability and correctness; then investigate throughput and latency. That order avoids turning an image-pull fix into an unsupported hardware recommendation.

sections.heading: When the old environment must remain
paragraphs: If your hardware or host cannot support the new documented stack, assess a supported older release or another maintained deployment path. Do not force an incompatible image into production because its version number is newer. The right outcome is a supported, reproducible service with known limits, not a successful download followed by unexplained crashes.

faqs.question: Does vLLM 0.34 still publish the old ROCm 7.2 artefacts?
faqs.answer: Its release notes say ROCm 7.2 artefacts were dropped in favour of the documented ROCm 10.0 wheels and images. Follow that release's exact installation matrix rather than guessing a replacement tag.

faqs.question: Does pulling an image prove my GPU is supported?
faqs.answer: No. Pulling proves that an artefact is available. Driver, hardware, runtime and model compatibility still require separate checks and an actual smoke test.

faqs.question: Why record an image digest instead of only a tag?
faqs.answer: A digest identifies a particular image content. Keeping it with the configuration and model revision makes a working deployment easier to reproduce and roll back.

title: Ollama Environment Variables on Windows: Why Your Changes Did Not Apply
searchTitle: Ollama Windows Environment Variables: Restart the Right Process
excerpt: Ollama ignores a new environment variable on Windows? Check the running process, user context and restart path before changing networking or model storage.

cover.alt: A pixel-art Windows workstation passes a new configuration card to a restarted application while an older process keeps its previous card.
cover.caption: Original GPT-generated pixel-art editorial illustration; conceptual artwork, not a product screenshot or test result.

intro: On Windows, Ollama inherits user and system environment variables when its process starts. Changing a variable in Settings does not rewrite the environment of an already-running application. If a documented setting appears ignored, quit Ollama fully, save the variable in the intended account context, and start the app again using the documented Windows procedure.
journalNote: This guide is about process inheritance, not a private deployment incident. The example checks one non-sensitive setting and avoids dumping a developer machine's entire environment into logs or public support threads.

sections.heading: Find the process that is actually serving requests
paragraphs: First determine whether you use the Windows desktop app, a manually launched server, a service wrapper or a container. Those launch paths can inherit configuration differently. A setting changed for your interactive account may not apply to a process started under another account or a container configuration.

Also check whether an older instance is still running. Starting another shell and setting a variable there does not necessarily replace the background app answering requests. Use supported application controls to quit and restart the intended process rather than killing unrelated processes indiscriminately.

sections.heading: Distinguish variable scope from variable spelling
paragraphs: Check the exact documented variable name and accepted value for your installed version. Then inspect where you set it. In PowerShell, the process environment is visible through the Env provider; user and machine values can also be inspected explicitly. Do not confuse a correctly spelled value in one scope with proof that another process inherited it.

These commands inspect values, not the complete running server state. Do not publish private hostnames in their output. If you use another variable containing sensitive data, avoid printing it at all; verify behaviour through a safe supported diagnostic instead.

A browser refresh is not a server restart. Nor does closing a terminal necessarily stop an independently running desktop application. The process that receives the request must be the one started after the new configuration became available.

paragraphs: Choose a supported check tied to the setting you changed. For a model directory change, inspect the documented storage behaviour and installed model availability. For a connection setting, confirm the intended local endpoint and client path. Do not expose the service on every network interface merely to prove that a configuration was read.

Record the installed version, setting name, launch method and observed result. Keep secret values out of the record. If the value is accepted but the behaviour still differs, inspect whether another configuration source, instance or client route explains the discrepancy.

sections.heading: Avoid turning a scope problem into a networking problem
paragraphs: A common wrong turn is broadening OLLAMA_HOST or allowing every browser origin because a client cannot connect. Those changes affect exposure and browser access, not simply environment inheritance. First verify which process is running and which address the client is using.

Similarly, increasing queue or context settings without confirming the active process can create confusion: the new value may not be in effect, or it may take effect later after an unrelated restart. Make one deliberate change and verify it before adjusting capacity controls.

sections.heading: Keep a small working configuration record
paragraphs: The general lesson applies to many developer tools: configuration is data consumed by a process at a particular time and scope. Checking that consumption is more useful than repeatedly typing the same value into different windows.

faqs.question: Why did editing an Ollama environment variable have no effect?
faqs.answer: An already-running process can retain its previous environment. Confirm the correct user context, quit Ollama fully and restart it using the documented Windows procedure.

faqs.question: Does setting a variable in PowerShell update every running app?
faqs.answer: No. A process-scoped setting affects that shell and processes it launches. It does not rewrite the environment of an existing Ollama desktop process or a separate service.

faqs.question: Should I post all environment variables in a bug report?
faqs.answer: No. Inspect only the relevant non-sensitive variable and sanitise the output. A full environment dump can contain credentials and unrelated private configuration.

title: Local-Only Ollama: Disable Cloud Features and Check the Request Path
searchTitle: Local-Only Ollama: Disable Cloud and Verify the Request Path
excerpt: Run Ollama with cloud features disabled, then verify the selected model and request route. Local configuration is one layer of a wider data-handling check.

cover.alt: A pixel-art local AI workstation inside a private room with its cloud route visibly switched off and a short internal request cable.
cover.caption: Original GPT-generated pixel-art editorial illustration; conceptual artwork, not a product screenshot or test result.

intro: Ollama can run local models and also offers cloud capabilities, so a localhost address alone does not prove every inference stays on your hardware. Its documentation provides a cloud-disable setting. Apply it through the correct launch path, restart, then verify the selected model and application route using a harmless request.
journalNote: This article explains a local-processing check, not a complete privacy certification. It does not claim that disabling one product feature prevents every other application, extension or tool on a computer from sending data elsewhere.

sections.heading: Define the boundary you need
paragraphs: Local-only can mean different things: model inference on your machine, no cloud model fallback, no prompt logging outside the device, or no network access at all. Write down the requirement. Disabling a cloud feature addresses a narrower boundary than isolating an entire machine from the network.

Also identify the full application. A browser interface, agent, model runtime and MCP tools may each have separate routes. The local model can stay local while a web-search tool intentionally sends a query to another service. That is not necessarily a defect, but it must match the requirement you are making.

sections.heading: Apply the documented cloud-disable control
paragraphs: Ollama's FAQ documents a server configuration setting and an environment-variable option. Use the path appropriate to your platform and launcher, then restart the relevant process. Do not overwrite an existing configuration file without preserving other intentional settings.

The documented environment alternative is OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1. On Windows, an already-running application can retain its old environment, so follow the quit-and-restart procedure. On services and containers, use their own supported environment configuration rather than a value set only in an unrelated shell.

For a stronger isolation requirement, use a supported restricted environment and test what still works. Separate model inference from activities that legitimately need network access, such as downloading a model. A successful offline test after preparation is evidence about that setup; it is not a claim that every installation or update operation works offline.

sections.heading: Review the surrounding data paths
paragraphs: Inspect conversation storage, browser extensions, application logs and connected tools. A local inference setting does not delete earlier cloud conversations or change another vendor's retention policy. If data was previously sent elsewhere, handle deletion and retention through that service's documented controls.

Keep the model server on the intended network boundary. Publishing an unauthenticated local endpoint can create a different exposure even when inference itself stays on your GPU. Local processing and safe network access are related but distinct design questions.

sections.heading: State the result with its scope
paragraphs: A useful conclusion is specific: under this version and configuration, this client used this local model with cloud features disabled, and this harmless request followed the intended route. A claim that no data can ever leave the computer would require a much broader review.

Recheck after changing clients, models, tool integrations or fallback settings. The purpose is a repeatable boundary you can explain, not a one-time privacy badge that survives every later configuration change.

faqs.question: How does Ollama document disabling cloud features?
faqs.answer: Its FAQ documents disable_ollama_cloud in the server configuration or OLLAMA_NO_CLOUD=1, followed by a restart. Use the platform-specific setup instructions and confirm the resulting behaviour.

faqs.question: Does localhost guarantee local model inference?
faqs.answer: No. A local service can route a request elsewhere. Check the selected model, cloud settings and actual application path rather than inferring data location from the hostname alone.

faqs.question: Is this a complete data privacy audit?
faqs.answer: No. It covers an Ollama configuration and request-path check. Other clients, telemetry, tools, logs and external services need their own review.

title: Ollama Is Using the CPU: Check Model Placement Before Buying a GPU
searchTitle: Ollama Using CPU? Check GPU Placement Before Upgrading
excerpt: Ollama is running on CPU? Inspect ollama ps, model placement, supported hardware and memory pressure before buying a GPU or changing drivers.

cover.alt: A pixel-art model workload is split between a CPU desk and a GPU station while a technician inspects the actual route.
cover.caption: Original GPT-generated pixel-art editorial illustration; conceptual artwork, not a product screenshot or test result.

intro: Before assuming Ollama is ignoring your GPU, inspect where the active model is loaded. The documented ollama ps output includes a PROCESSOR column that can show CPU, GPU or a split. That observation is more useful than guessing from fan noise, a download size or the presence of a GPU in the computer.
journalNote: This guide is about diagnosing placement rather than recommending hardware from an invented fit chart. No model-to-GPU capacity results or tokens-per-second measurements are claimed here.

sections.heading: Make the intended model active
paragraphs: Send a small harmless request using the client you are investigating. Then inspect the active models using Ollama's documented command. This connects the observation to a particular request rather than an idle system where the model may already have unloaded.

Read the PROCESSOR column using the current documentation. Fully GPU, fully CPU and split placement describe different states. Record the model identity and version privately if needed. Do not publish unrelated local model names or a full machine diagnostic dump just to ask a placement question.

sections.heading: Check supported hardware and the actual runtime
paragraphs: Use Ollama's current hardware and platform guidance for your GPU and operating system. A device being visible to the desktop does not establish that the inference runtime supports it through the selected backend. If you use a container or service, verify that it can access the intended device in that environment.

Check installation and driver guidance from the relevant official vendors. Avoid downloading a driver bundle or performance patch from a random model-speed video. Do not change several runtime layers at once; preserve the previous working setup and record each targeted change.

paragraphs: The model's weights are only part of the runtime budget. Context-related state, active requests, execution overhead and other processes can consume memory. A configuration that fully offloads one short request can behave differently with longer contexts or multiple loaded models.

Inspect what else is using the GPU before assuming the model alone explains placement. Another inference service or notebook can reduce available memory. On a shared system, identify the owner of a process rather than terminating it without context. The relevant number is available memory under the actual workload, not only the device's advertised capacity.

sections.heading: Reduce the workload before changing hardware
paragraphs: Try a supported smaller model or a shorter bounded request as an isolation experiment. Keep the client and runtime constant. If placement changes, you have evidence that model or workload size matters; you have not yet proved a universal capacity threshold.

Then vary context and concurrency deliberately. Do not interpret a faster short response as proof that a model is better for your coding tasks. Preserve quality checks too. A model that returns less output or skips required reasoning may look fast while failing the task.

sections.heading: Measure the performance question separately
paragraphs: Once placement is understood, measure first-token delay, post-first-token timing and total completion time under a declared workload. Keep cold loading separate from warm inference. Report failed requests, not just the fastest successful answer.

A single tokens-per-second number cannot explain whether time was spent loading the model, processing a long prompt, waiting in a queue or generating output. The separate benchmark-method article gives a timing fixture and definitions without inventing hardware results.

sections.heading: Decide what evidence justifies an upgrade
paragraphs: A purchase decision needs your required model, context, concurrency, supported runtime and acceptable latency. Check current vendor specifications and independent tests that disclose their conditions. Do not extrapolate a smaller model's fit from a file-size ratio alone.

If it does not, you now have a concrete capacity and responsiveness requirement to research. That is a stronger basis for spending money than an idle GPU graph or a generic recommendation list.

faqs.question: Does a model fitting on disk mean it fits in VRAM?
faqs.answer: No. Runtime representation, context-related state and other allocations matter. Disk file size is not a complete GPU-memory requirement.

faqs.question: Should I buy a new GPU immediately when inference is slow?
faqs.answer: First verify placement, supported hardware, active workload and memory pressure. Slow output can have several causes, and a hardware purchase should follow evidence about your actual requirements.

intro: Ollama documents a 503 overloaded response when too many requests reach its queue. That is different from proving the process is dead. paragraphs: A reverse proxy, application gateway and model runtime can all return server errors. Retain the status and a sanitised response summary so you can identify the source. A generic frontend message saying unavailable hides whether the model queue is full, a gateway timed out or the process cannot be reached.

Keep request identifiers non-sensitive and do not log entire conversations by default. Correlate the failing time with supported runtime logs and active-request observations. If the process responds with an overload message, that is evidence of a live but constrained path, not proof that restarting it is the right remedy.

sections.heading: Inspect offered load, not only completed work
paragraphs: Count attempts, active requests, queued work and failures over the same interval. A UI with a retry loop can offer much more work than the number of people using it suggests. Multiple tabs, background jobs and another local client can also share the runtime.

Review whether a large context or long output keeps a request active for a long time. Capacity depends on workload shape. Ten short requests and ten long-context generations are not equivalent experiments. Keep the model and settings fixed while investigating that difference.

paragraphs: Classify retryable overload separately from invalid input, unsupported models and permission failures. Give automatic retries a maximum attempt count and elapsed-time budget. Add jitter where many clients could retry together. A cancel action should stop future attempts rather than merely hiding the spinner.

Be careful after a timeout: the server may still be processing the original request. Starting another attempt can duplicate expensive work. For workflows with side effects, use application-level operation identity and verification; a chat-generation retry and a payment or database-write retry do not have the same consequences.

paragraphs: A busy state can say that the local model is handling other work and offer cancellation or a later retry. Do not show a success message until a result arrives. Avoid an endless spinner that conceals repeated failures or a button that silently submits the same request several times.

faqs.question: Does an Ollama 503 mean the server has crashed?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Ollama documents an overloaded response for excess queued requests. Identify the responding component and inspect load before treating it as a dead process.

faqs.question: Will increasing OLLAMA_MAX_QUEUE make generation faster?
faqs.answer: No. A larger waiting queue is not additional compute capacity. It can trade earlier rejection for longer waits and must be evaluated alongside latency and memory behaviour.

faqs.question: Should my UI retry every failed request automatically?
faqs.answer: No. Use a bounded policy for appropriate transient failures, preserve cancellation, and consider whether an upstream timeout leaves the request outcome uncertain. Do not retry permanent or oversized requests indefinitely.

intro: DeepSeek's public chat demo is useful for exploring its APIs, but a personal bring-your-own-key demo and a public product have different security requirements. The guide says the demo stores the API key, conversations and uploaded images in the browser. That does not mean a shared product key should be bundled into frontend code.

sections.heading: Start with the demo's stated purpose
paragraphs: The official guide provides a chat client to demonstrate features such as streaming, file input and web tools. It describes browser storage for the key and conversation-related data. Read that statement with its scope: where the demo persists data is not the same as where an API processes a request.

For a personal experiment, a user may deliberately supply their own key. For a public product, the developer may instead pay for requests through a shared service account. Those are different ownership and abuse models. Copying the visual interface does not resolve the change in responsibility.

sections.heading: A frontend build cannot keep a shared secret
paragraphs: Anything delivered to the browser must be treated as available to the person running it. Renaming a variable, minifying a bundle or hiding a button does not create a secret boundary. Build-time environment variables that become JavaScript are configuration delivery, not a backend vault.

In a public service architecture, a controlled server receives the application request and calls the provider using its protected credential. That server still needs authentication or another deliberate access policy, input limits, rate limits and cost controls. Moving a key to a server is necessary for that model, but it is not the whole security design.

paragraphs: List each data class: credential, prompt, response, uploaded file, error log and analytics event. If web tools fetch pages or documents are uploaded, those operations introduce additional processing. Review the relevant provider documentation and your own interface copy. Do not promise that deleting a browser conversation removes every provider-side file or log unless the documented controls and your implementation establish that result.

paragraphs: Use invented prompts and a disposable development configuration. Inspect the browser bundle to confirm that no shared credential was built into it. Check network requests and error handling without copying authentication headers into public screenshots.

paragraphs: The demo is valuable as a feature map and a public reference implementation. Study how it presents streamed answers, sources and file states. faqs.answer: No. Local storage location and inference processing location are different. The API must receive the request needed to generate an answer; review the provider's current data-handling terms.

faqs.question: Can I place a shared DeepSeek API key in a frontend environment variable?
faqs.answer: No. Values bundled into browser code can be read by visitors. A shared service credential belongs on a controlled backend, with appropriate authentication and usage limits.

faqs.question: Is the public chat demo a complete production architecture?
faqs.answer: Its documentation describes it as a demonstration. Use it to understand features, then separately design the credential, authorisation, retention, abuse and cost controls your product needs.

paragraphs: The fixture can contain a plain sentence telling the assistant to perform an unrelated mock action. It should be visibly part of the retrieved document, not a real instruction from the user. Keep it harmless and easy to recognise so the test's purpose is unambiguous.

Treat retrieved pages, repository files and tool outputs as untrusted data. A tool result can be relevant evidence without being allowed to change the assistant's rules. This distinction should be reflected in both the prompt structure and the application's capabilities.

sections.heading: Use the result to improve the system
paragraphs: If the agent follows the document instruction, narrow the tool surface and review how trusted instructions and data are represented. If application enforcement blocks the action, preserve that protection rather than relaxing it to make the agent appear capable. If the agent reports a false outcome, add state verification before final success messages.

OWASP's agentic security guidance is a useful framework for this layered review. The practical lesson is testable: untrusted content should not gain authority merely because a trusted tool delivered it. Prove that with harmless fixtures and actual action evidence.

references.label: OWASP: Securing Agentic Applications V2, November 10

faqs.question: What is the safe way to test this injection boundary?
faqs.answer: Use a disposable environment, invented document text and a mock tool that records calls without external effects. Define allowed and forbidden actions before running the test.

faqs.question: Does a refusal sentence prove the agent did nothing unsafe?
faqs.answer: No. Inspect the tool trace and actual mock state too. An agent can describe a refusal after already attempting an action or can report success without a real effect.

faqs.question: Can a prompt replace server-side tool permissions?
faqs.answer: No. Instructions help guide behaviour, while the application must still enforce authorisation, validate arguments and restrict what tools can do.

title: RAG Data Retention: Deleting a File Is Not the Same as Removing Every Copy
searchTitle: RAG Data Retention: Delete Sources and Derived Copies
excerpt: Deleting a RAG source file may leave chunks, embeddings, caches and backups. Map the lifecycle and test removal across retrieval and application storage.

cover.alt: A pixel-art document branches into chunk shelves, a vector index and cache drawers, with a careful deletion checklist following every branch.
cover.caption: Original GPT-generated pixel-art editorial illustration; conceptual artwork, not a product screenshot or test result.

intro: Deleting an uploaded file is not automatically the same as removing every copy used by a RAG system. Parsed text, chunks, embeddings, caches, conversation excerpts and backups can have different lifecycles. Build a data map, define a deletion contract and test that removed material no longer appears in authorised retrieval.
journalNote: The document identifiers and retention scenarios here are invented. This is a general engineering design, not a disclosure of UltraFit360's storage layout or a legal assurance about any provider's deletion policy.

sections.heading: Draw the lifecycle before writing the delete handler
paragraphs: List the original upload, parsed output, chunks, embeddings, metadata, retrieval cache, generated answers, logs and backups that your system actually uses. Identify owners and retention rules. Do not add imaginary stores merely to make the diagram complex, but do not omit a cache because it feels temporary.

For each store, ask how a source is identified and how its version is represented. If the original file is renamed, its derived chunks should not become untraceable. A stable internal identity makes lifecycle operations more reliable than searching for a filename string later.

sections.heading: Carry source identity into derived records
paragraphs: An invented chunk record might include a source ID, version, chunk ID and access scope. The exact schema depends on your system, but the relationship should support removal and reindexing. Avoid storing a private path as the only link between a vector and its source.

Separate deletion of one version from deletion of the entire source. Replacing a document can leave older chunks retrievable unless the ingestion workflow retires them explicitly. Also consider duplicate uploads: two files with similar text may represent separate authorised objects or accidental copies.

sections.heading: Define what the user-facing promise means
paragraphs: Does Remove mean hide from this workspace, stop future retrieval, delete active storage or start a broader deletion process? Use language that matches the implementation and provider terms. Do not promise immediate erasure from every backup if the documented lifecycle does not support that statement.
